writing_manner.reasoning: The candidate did real rewriting — the source's numbered instruction lists inside each phase were dissolved into running declarative prose, and the standalone Guardrails block disappeared. But the source's presentational skeleton survives intact: an H1 title, one H2 per stage in the source's order, bold run-in labels for the two verifiers, and two inline code spans carrying literal JSON schemas. The reference has no headings, no bold, no code spans and no title at all — it opens straight into scoping sentences and marks its stages with bare numbers. Several candidate sentences also coordinate three or four responsibilities into one clause chain, where the reference gives each responsibility its own short sentence. This is anchor 3: register broadly right, source artifacts persist.

altitude.reasoning: The single largest gap. The reference stops at the responsibility and pushes every shape into contracts.py: no filenames, no log files, no directory tree, no field names, no status enums. The candidate retains essentially the whole mechanical layer of the source — the workspace tree with `task.md` / `status.md` / `iter-N/`, the report filenames, 'absolute paths', 'appends to its log as it works', the concrete agent type `general-purpose`, and both verifier JSON schemas reproduced field-for-field including their status enums. The Decide stage is the one stage close to reference altitude, and even it reaches back down into the JSON with `overall == "pass"`. That is anchor 2: one stage at reference level, several at source level.

conditions.reasoning: The decision itself is well formed and is the candidate's closest match to the reference: a stated clean predicate followed by a closed three-way bulleted set, each branch naming its condition, its action, and whether work continues. Two things pull it down. The cap branch carries an open-ended escape — 'Continuing needs the user's permission' — which opens a fourth path (permission granted, loop continues past 5) that is never declared, and which the reference deliberately does not have: its result type admits only Passed or Stopped(cap_reached). And the loop limit is only discoverable from inside the branches, whereas the reference states it once up front as a standing constraint before any stage.

structures.reasoning: Most of the reference's declarative apparatus is absent. The frontmatter is the source's verbatim — name and description only, with no inputs, no official output, no types file and no workspace declaration; the workspace is instead narrated in the body. There is no types file at all, so the domain types are described inline as raw JSON literals. No result is declared with a `(→ Type)` marker anywhere; results are expressed as 'Writes <filename>'. Two devices do survive: parallelism is announced before the subagents that perform it, and each subagent is given a role and its work. That leaves the body only partly declarative — the labelled roles and the bulleted closed decision are real structure, so this is not bare prose, but the contract, the result declarations and the types file are all missing.

coverage.reasoning: Nothing the reference carries is dropped and nothing is invented — the loop, the two verifier roles with their distinct criteria, the three-way decision, the fixer's evidence discipline and the terminal report are all present. The failure is the timid-sculpt one: four outcome-bearing responsibilities the source carried and the reference deliberately compressed away are retained. (1) Per-phase progress reporting to the user plus a running `status.md` — the reference removed user reporting entirely and reports only the terminal result. (2) Surfacing silent subagent failure from an empty log. (3) The worker's 'must not self-verify' prohibition, which the reference lets the separate verifier subagents imply. (4) The permission escape above the cap. A run of this skill would emit progress reports the reference's run would not, and could exceed five iterations. The reference's one scoping addition — that the workspace does not confine task effects — is absent here, but it is an interpretation limit rather than an outcome, so I did not count it as a drop.

what_to_fix_in_the_sculpting_skill: The skill needs a hard rule that the sculpted frontmatter is a contract — it must declare inputs, the official output, the path to a types file, and a workspace when a result is saved — and a companion rule that every named data shape (field lists, status enums, serialisation formats, report filenames) is moved into that types file and referenced from the body only via a `(→ Type)` result marker. This is the single missing rule that drives three of the five deductions at once: with no types file to move shapes into, this candidate had nowhere to put the two verifier JSON schemas or the report filenames, so they stayed inline in the body (altitude 2), the `(→ Type)` device was never available (structures 2), and the body had to keep code spans and bold labels to carry them (writing manner 3). A secondary rule worth adding: when the source states a limit with an escape clause ('max N without user permission'), the sculpt keeps the limit and drops the escape unless the escape's branch is itself declared — otherwise the closed decision leaks an undeclared path.
